candidates.title: PRT bridge refetches and reprocesses every log of the shared tournament factory, so each epoch observation (and every match's response) slows with unrelated chain activity and permissionless instantiate() spam
candidates.component: PRT player and bridge (doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua observe/refresh/jobs, prt-log-history.lua, used by crisium.lua and prt-epoch.lua)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'); stands in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:observe lines 57-68 (addresses = {self.factory, self.consensus, self.root}, get_logs_of with no topics), 110-179 (table.sort of all logs and per-log loop on every observation), methods:jobs 373 (iterates snapshot.events), methods:refresh 337-344 and methods:attempt 601 (observation repeated per tick and per attempt); doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua 106-130 (factory = consensus.getTournamentFactory(), first_block = seal_block); doc/recipes/crisium.lua 124 (factory read from DaveConsensus); Dave DaveAppFactory.sol (one immutable TOURNAMENT_FACTORY shared by every app); MultiLevelTournamentFactory.instantiate (permissionless, emits TournamentCreated with no indexed field).
candidates.description: The bridge needs from the factory only the TournamentCreated log of its own root tournament (to get the descriptor and bond). It nevertheless fetches every log the factory emits from the epoch's seal block up to the observed head, keeps them in its history for the life of the epoch, and on every observation sorts and walks all of them and appends them to snapshot.events, which jobs() walks again. The factory is shared by every Dave application on the chain (DaveAppFactory passes one immutable TOURNAMENT_FACTORY to each DaveConsensus) and its instantiate() is permissionless. So the per-observation work of the honest player's bridge grows linearly (sort: n log n) with the TournamentCreated logs of other applications' epochs and of any spam, i.e. with chain activity that does not belong to the application. prt-epoch.lua deliberately filters the shared InputBox by the application's topic ('The InputBox is shared by every application, so only this application's inputs are fetched') but the factory gets no such filter (and cannot be filtered by topic, since TournamentCreated has no indexed field; the root's creation is in the seal block, which the bridge already knows). Every match of the epoch is answered only after a full observation (refresh() runs at each tick and again inside attempt() before each transaction), so the cost of processing data that belongs to other applications/tournaments delays every move of the honest commitment, and prt-lua-bridge.md states that 'confirmation delay, computation, RPC latency, and inclusion delay must together fit the windows the events give'.
candidates.trigger: Anyone: other Dave applications sharing the factory create a root per epoch (benign background growth), and an adversary can call MultiLevelTournamentFactory.instantiate(anyHash, anyProvider) repeatedly during an open epoch (estimated ~0.2M gas per call, not measured) to add TournamentCreated logs that every honest bridge of that chain must fetch and re-sort on every observation.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on any deployment where the factory is the shared one returned by DaveConsensus.getTournamentFactory() (the configuration crisium.lua and prt-deploy.lua use). The adversary capability 'Raise activity on the chain that does not belong to the application' (THREAT_MODEL section 7) covers the spam; no guest or emulator condition is needed.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No exclusion applies: the trigger is chain activity outside the application, an adversary capability of section 7 ('Raise activity on the chain that does not belong to the application, such as inputs to other applications that share its input record'). Not a validator node (sling / Rollups Node) and not a test harness.

2 Role: the PRT bridge/player is Support per AUDIT.md ('No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI'). It stands in for the honest operator ('implementations of an operator that no deployment runs'), so section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'.

3 High/Medium cases: as a support defect it lands on the support Medium case if the honest-operator rating is High/Critical. Among High cases, 'a defect that lets ... host load ... multiply the worst-case cost ... by a constant factor' does not fit, because the growth is unbounded in the number of foreign logs, not a constant factor.

4 Critical (in the stood-in role): R12 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain ... has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match, and its total grows only with the inputs, yields, and matches of the epochs still open. That total must not grow with the application's age, with the number of past epochs, or with chain activity that does not belong to the application.' Each observation's cost here grows with foreign factory logs. A8 'Failing to process one match's data, for any reason, must not stop, delay or decide any other match' is touched in the sense that processing other tournaments' data delays every match's response. Critical for an honest-operator component -> Medium for this support component.
5 Low: not applicable unless triage holds that the stood-in role is not the honest operator; then Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: The goal assumes the honest operator 'submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'. An operator built like this bridge spends a growing, adversary-inflatable share of every response window re-reading foreign factory logs before it can answer any of its matches; with enough foreign logs (other apps over a long dispute, or spam) observations take seconds to minutes, eating response budgets and, in the limit, making the honest claim lose by timeout, after which a dishonest claim can win. It also grows memory for the life of the epoch.
candidates.evidence: Mock-chain experiment /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/A8/factory-spam.lua (run with bugs/env.sh, lua5.4): a bridge observer whose factory stream holds N extra TournamentCreated logs of other tournaments, after the root's creation. Observed per-observation logs/events and CPU: N=0 -> 2 logs, 0.000 s; N=10,000 -> 10,002 logs, 0.07 s repeat observation; N=100,000 -> 100,002 logs, 1.1 s repeat (1.8 s first); N=300,000 -> 300,002 logs, 3.4 s repeat (5.8 s first). Every foreign log appears in snapshot.logs and snapshot.events of every observation, even with the history cached. Real ABI decoding and RPC transfer add to this; refresh() runs more than once per tick.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test with a mock chain (as in prt-bridge-test.lua): build a bridge (or observer) whose factory stream contains the root's TournamentCreated in the seal block plus K TournamentCreated logs of other tournaments in later blocks; assert that the logs the bridge requests and the size of snapshot.logs/snapshot.events after observe() do not depend on K (e.g. equal for K=0 and K=1000), i.e. that the factory is read only at the seal block or the root descriptor is read with tournamentDescriptor()/bondValue() calls. On audit/prt2 the counts grow with K (exit 1).

candidates.title: One leaf match whose native and Solidity proof checks disagree crashes the whole PRT player by assert, and the crash repeats on every restart, so every other match, cleanup and epoch stops
candidates.component: PRT player and bridge (doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:attempt / methods:prepare; doc/recipes/crisium.lua main loop)
candidates.role: Support (stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua lines 509-522 (prepare winLeafMatch: proof_check from pcall(eth.verify_transition)), 620-639 (attempt: assert(not failure or failure.code == 3, "proof simulation RPC failure") and assert(transaction.proof_check.valid == (failure == nil), "native and Solidity transition verification disagree")); also prt-transactions.lua 220, 228, 235 (asserts on preflight/estimate failures and 'estimated transaction exceeds block gas limit'); crisium.lua pass() 296-315 (one process ticks every epoch's bridge, no per-epoch/per-job isolation) and the supervisor relaunch (prt-supervise.sh).
candidates.description: For winLeafMatch the bridge checks the proof natively (C++/Lua verifiers) and by simulating the Solidity call, and turns any disagreement between the two into a Lua assert. The assert is not caught anywhere: it propagates out of tick() and pass() and terminates the player process. Because prepared transactions are rebuilt deterministically from the chain and the stored epoch, the relaunched player reaches the same job, recomputes the same proof and asserts again, so the process never gets past it. All other work of the account is in the same process and loop: the honest commitment's moves in every other tournament of the epoch (and in a later epoch, once settled bridges and live bridges coexist), the permissionless cleanup that lets the root tournament finish, staging and bond recovery. The failure of one match's processing therefore stops all other matches instead of marking that one job invalid (the bridge already has self.invalid for the case where both checks reject). The same pattern applies to the other asserts on per-job external responses in submit() (preflight or estimate errors other than code 3, a gas estimate above the block gas limit).
candidates.trigger: Any disagreement between the off-chain verifiers and the deployed CartesiStateTransition on one leaf proof (e.g. an R2/R3 divergence between the C++ verify functions and the regenerated solidity-step, such as the halt/overflow precedence and TLB-index changes noted in bugs/harness/README.md), or an RPC that answers the simulation with a non-revert error; the dispute position is steered by the adversary ('Steer the dispute to any position of the honest computation').
candidates.reachability: Needs a pre-existing divergence between the native and Solidity verification at some reachable position, or an RPC error; I did not demonstrate such a divergence. Given one, an adversary can steer a match to that position, after which the player crash-loops.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No listed exclusion; not a validator node or test harness. The trigger is a verifier divergence or a node RPC error, not an untrusted API caller.
2 Role: Support (AUDIT.md). Stands in for the honest operator. Off-chain verifiers are Support too ('Off-chain verifiers ... Support').

3 High/Medium cases: no listed High/Medium case covers 'a crash that turns one match's failure into a stop of all matches'. If the trigger is counted as 'data from other parties that the honest operator may decline' (a leaf proof only verified for its own information), the stood-in rating is High ('A crash ... in a component in the honest-operator role, caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline') -> support Medium.

4 Critical (in the stood-in role): A8 'Failing to process one match's data, for any reason, must not stop, delay or decide any other match.' and R4 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim.' The crash loop stops every other match and the honest defence of later epochs. Critical in the honest-operator role -> Medium for support. If triage requires the trigger itself (a verifier divergence) to be shown reachable first, the divergence would be the primary defect and this is its amplifier.
5 Low: if triage holds that a crash which needs a pre-existing verifier divergence violates nothing on its own, Low.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Low if the triggering divergence is not shown)
candidates.threat_to_goal: An honest operator built this way stops defending every claim, and stops the cleanup that ends the tournament, as soon as one leaf proof of one match fails to process, and cannot recover by restarting. Its other claims can then be eliminated by timeout, so a dishonest claim can win. A8 requires the failure to stay confined to that match.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only (no run): both asserts sit in methods:attempt between the simulation and the submission, outside any pcall; crisium.lua's main loop does 'assert(not status.terminal, status.terminal)' and has no pcall around pass(); prt-supervise.sh relaunches from the same stored state.
candidates.test_idea: Unit test with the mock chain of prt-bridge-test.lua: a LeafMatchSealed job held by the player whose native verification passes while chain:simulate returns { code = 3 } (or the reverse). Required behavior: tick() returns normally, the job is marked invalid or reported as an anomaly, and a second job in another match (e.g. an advanceMatch due in the same tick, or a cleanup) is still attempted. On audit/prt2 tick() raises 'native and Solidity transition verification disagree' (exit 1).

candidates.title: Referee model: logical time advances only after every connected player answers advance_time, so one silent or slow player, even one in no match, stalls every match and tournament
candidates.component: PRT referee model (doc/recipes/prt.lua referee over doc/recipes/game-transport.lua server)
candidates.role: Referee model (section 3: a defect that 'only crashes or stalls the model, even when that stops other matches (A8), is rated as support')
candidates.location: doc/recipes/game-transport.lua server_meta.__index.step_time 1062-1137 (self.batch with entry.pending[connection] = true for every connection from get_players(); clock:barrier_ready(self.batch) before any response is accepted or time moves), adopt() 564-603 (one outstanding event per connection; send_next_event only after its reply); doc/README.md 'Clocks and logical time' ('A player that connects and never answers therefore stalls the demonstration, where a blockchain would let its deadline pass').
candidates.description: Each block, the server sends advance_time to every connected player and advances neither its clock nor any match until every one of them has replied. A player that stays connected and never answers (or answers each advance_time after a long wall-clock delay) therefore freezes every match, every uarch tournament and the outputs phase, regardless of which match, if any, it plays in. Its own match is not the only one affected: matches between other claims, including the honest claim's, can never reach their deadlines, so a failure to process one party's traffic stops all matches. The manual documents the stall but does not list it among the model's non-normative simplifications (the closing paragraph lists the trusted single referee, bonds, pairing in rounds, direct uarch propagation and the leaf-proof window).
candidates.trigger: Any player (an adversary needs no claim) connects and stops replying to advance_time while keeping the socket open, or delays every reply.
candidates.reachability: Reachable with the shipped referee and any player; documented in the manual.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The test harnesses are out of scope, but prt.lua's referee and game-transport.lua are the referee model, which is in scope. The manual's listed simplifications are 'not normative', but this stall is not in that list; it is described in the clock section.
2 Role: Referee model. Section 3: 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond, or only crashes or stalls the model, even when that stops other matches (A8), is rated as support.'

3 High/Medium cases: as support, Medium only 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. A deployed referee whose matches all freeze when one party is silent would violate A8 for every match ('Failing to process one match's data, for any reason, must not stop ... any other match'), which is Critical; read that way, support Medium. Logical-time outcomes are not changed, so nothing is decided wrongly.
4 Critical: not applicable directly (support rating per section 3).
5 Low: if triage reads section 3 as making every stall of the model Low, or treats the documented stall as an accepted simplification, Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not change which claim wins; it lets one participant freeze the normative model's dispute, so the model cannot demonstrate A8 and a deployment modelled on it would be livelocked by one silent participant.
candidates.evidence: Code reading of step_time/barrier_ready and the manual statement quoted above; no run.
candidates.test_idea: Run the referee with the honest player plus one extra connection that announces a player role and never answers advance_time (game-test-server.lua style). Required: the honest claim's matches still progress and the tournament settles (e.g. the referee drops or times out the silent connection). On audit/prt2 the referee never advances past the first block (exit 1 after a wall-clock bound).

candidates.title: Bridge prefers an already pending cleanup transaction for another match over a newly due, deadline-bound move of the honest commitment, so the cleanup's mining delays the honest response
candidates.component: PRT player and bridge (doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:tick, prt-transactions.lua submit)
candidates.role: Support (stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:tick 720-746 (selected = the pending candidate's job whenever it is still eligible, overriding eligible[1], the earliest-expiry job) and 747-783 (only the selected job is attempted); prt-transactions.lua submit 184-191 (a same-job resubmission waits bump_blocks before re-pricing) and 140-154 (15% bumps); also tick 725-727 (a pending transaction of another epoch's bridge is never replaced).
candidates.description: Jobs are sorted by expiry, but once the account has a pending transaction for some job, tick() keeps selecting that job as long as it is still eligible ('Keep working on a useful pending action. Do not oscillate'), and attempts no other job. A permissionless cleanup such as eliminateMatchByTimeout or eliminateInnerTournament of an adversary-vs-adversary match has an open-ended window (last = maxinteger), so it stays eligible until its deletion is observed. If such a cleanup is pending when a deadline-bound move of the honest commitment becomes due (advanceMatch, seal, winLeafMatch, winInnerTournament before winnerExpiresAt), the honest move is not even prepared or published until the cleanup transaction is mined; the cleanup is only re-priced every bump_blocks. Replacing the pending cleanup with the urgent move at the same nonce would publish the urgent move at once. Likewise, the live epoch's bridge never replaces a pending transaction of a settled epoch's bridge (e.g. a tryRecoveringBond with no deadline). Processing another match's (or epoch's) transaction thus delays the honest commitment's own match.
candidates.trigger: Adversary-vs-adversary matches that reach their elimination instant while the honest commitment's own turn comes up (the adversary controls both timings), together with any inclusion delay of the cleanup transaction (fee rises, congestion).
candidates.reachability: Reachable whenever the honest bridge runs with cleanup (the default) and the adversary times an eliminable match of its own just before the honest commitment's turn; the delay is bounded by how long the cleanup takes to be mined (one block on an idle chain, several bump intervals under rising fees).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No exclusion; not a validator node or test harness.
2 Role: Support (AUDIT.md), standing in for the honest operator.

3 High/Medium cases: none of the listed High/Medium cases names transaction scheduling. If counted as host load multiplying a cost by a constant factor, the stood-in rating would be High -> support Medium.

4 Critical (in the stood-in role): A8 'Failing to process one match's data, for any reason, must not stop, delay or decide any other match' (a stuck transaction of another match delays this one) and R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'. If the delay can exceed the response budget the stood-in rating is Critical -> support Medium.
5 Low: if the delay is judged to stay within the response budget in every case, it is a priority inversion with no rule violated: Low.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Medium if the delay can exceed a response window)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It spends part of the honest claim's response window on an unrelated transaction. Under fee pressure, or with a short response budget, the honest move can miss its deadline and the honest claim lose by timeout.
candidates.test_idea: Mock-chain unit test: the journal reports a pending candidate whose job is an eliminateMatchByTimeout that is still eligible, and the snapshot also has an advanceMatch job for the honest commitment with an earlier expiry. Required: tick() attempts the advanceMatch (and replaces the pending candidate). On audit/prt2 it attempts only the cleanup (exit 1).

not_covered: Dave Tournament.sol / MatchClocks / Clock were read for cross-match coupling (shared matchCount, dangling commitment, inner-tournament propagation, timeout classifier, asserts on progress paths, refunds, provider coupling through DaveConsensus._inputIndexLowerBound). I found no A8 defect, but I did not run any of these on-chain or fuzz them, and I did not quantify how far adversary-vs-adversary matches can push the root tournament's finish (and so the next epoch's start), which is an A7 sizing question.
Economic coupling across matches through the shared tournament balance (refunds paid from all joins' bonds draining the reserve that other matches' refunds rely on): not analysed in depth.
DaveConsensus staging and outputs-proof path (A5) and InputBox size limits (A3): only skimmed; they are other angles.
prt.lua referee-model rounds: next-round matches wait for the slowest match of the round. Not reported because the manual lists round-based pairing as a non-normative simplification.
prt.lua player internals (machine cache, forests, bundle replay, uarch claim build cost) as a source of cross-match delay: only the event handlers were read.
Restart interplay (crisium.lua plus prt-supervise.sh plus multiple epoch listeners) under kill -9: not exercised; the player-restart harness was not run.
crisium.lua seal_history keeps every consensus log since the application's deployment (grows with application age); judged negligible, not reported.
No experiment on the real chain harness (anvil plus Dave): gas cost of factory.instantiate spam and real RPC/ABI decoding cost per log were not measured.
game-transport.lua parsing of malformed or huge player messages (memory, JSON depth) as a way to stall the referee model: not examined.
